Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

musical adjective

of music; fond of music

also musically, a musical family, tuneful

classical

Cic. Leg. 2.39: lēgēs mūsicae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 52, 349

mūsicus, mūsica, mūsicum

of music, musical

Of music itself: īnstrūmentum mūsicum, lēgēs mūsicae, the rules of music. As a noun a musician (Cic. Off. 1.146); in Terence also of poetry (Lewis & Short). Of a person who loves music, Latin uses a phrase, as Pliny calls the dolphin mūsicae artī amīcum.

Other words

  • canōrus, canōra, canōrum — tuneful, melodious (of a voice or a sound)

    also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 234: vōce suāvī et canōrā (Lewis & Short)

    Of a voice or an instrument that sings well; of a speaker’s voice it can also be a fault, a sing-song (Cic. Off. 1.133, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • delphīnus nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī

    the dolphin, an animal friendly not only to man but also to musicPlin. NH 9.24

See also music, musical instrument, musical, sing.

SourcesLewis & Short: musicus · Lewis & Short: canorus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 52, 349.
